test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 17 March, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

A bite at the cherry

options.text: An attempt or opportunity to do something
To have a leverage over someone

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom** "A bite at the cherry"** is used to refer to an opportunity to achieve something or a chance to do something.
 
• **It often refers **to a second chance or another opportunity after missing out on a previous attempt.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:* 'An attempt or opportunity to do something.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are incorrect:

 
 
• **"A wrong move" -** This phrase means to make an incorrect decision or action, which does not relate to the concept of an opportunity presented in "a bite at the cherry."
 
• **"To have a leverage over someone" -** This phrase means to have a form of power or advantage over another person, which does not correspond with the idea of an opportunity or attempt expressed in the idiom.
 
• **"A dog bite" - **This is a literal translation and does not convey the metaphorical meaning of the idiom "a bite at the cherry," which is about opportunities or attempts, not about physical biting.
